description:
MEASURED at exact experiment base `40563eeb756636153df0aac67d01940864fe2556`; final review candidate is reconciled on warning-contract base `b5969795f8aaf2d3f39af7c822736a84da2b999f` (2026-09-06).

## Status

FINAL REVIEW CANDIDATE. The correct outcome is to retain the existing capture-tuple key and reject the additional flow-sensitive analysis.

## Goal, signal, strategy

Determine whether a non-recursive callable transporter can omit more capture information from its activation key while preserving dispatch-free static grounding. The signal is fewer semantic activations/executables without new runtime dispatch, widened capture lanes, semantic artifact movement, or disproportionate recurring compiler work. The strategy was TDD: pin the same-lambda int/float control and eight cost fixtures, prototype the smallest flow-sensitive projection in the existing demand lattice, then compare deterministic behavior, artifacts, claims, products, and scheduler work over the full corpus.

## Retained law

`World::canonical_activation_key` erases a transported closure brand but retains its capture tuple. After brand erasure, a context-free key cannot know whether two values came from the same or different lambdas. Whole-tuple or arity-only erasure therefore loses dispatch-free static grounding for the same lambda closed over one int versus one float; runtime construction dispatch must recover the distinction.

This is a conservative correct-by-construction/performance law. It is not a claim that tuple erasure changes program semantics or that every possible tuple component is universally necessary.

The static same-lambda fixture remains split by typed `FunctionId`/`Ty` capture layouts with no dispatch. Its dynamic twin correctly uses a nonempty two-arm construction dispatch. Display/canonical strings and incidental order are not semantic authorities.

## Rejected prototype

The prototype added capture-layout relevance as a fourth component of the one existing `InputDemand` fact and propagated it through the existing forwarding graph. It safely removed six executables and 89 product evaluations from actor_ring and the two mailbox-closure fixtures.

Across all 478 backend-producing fixtures, however, `work_graph.applied` rose `140,285 -> 143,458` (+3,173) while product evaluations fell only `172,177 -> 172,088` (-89). 448 fixtures did more work-graph applies; the remaining mover held applies flat while removing 31 product evaluations. No normalized behavior/exit status or root activation dump moved; 16 backend canons and 12 claim lifecycles are fully classified. The extra read/join/transform cost is disproportionate, so the prototype and fourth component were deleted. No production scaffolding lands.

## Eight-fixture proof and fixture collapse

All eight retained inventory paths are pinned at `26/153/31/41/24/166/237/237`. The former root-only `00275_enum_count_member_reduce.fz` is promoted to `fixtures2/behavior/enum_count_member_reduce.fz` with one adjacent Elixir oracle and stdout golden. Its weaker compile-only port test and runtime TODO are deleted. On the fz-kdt.185 base it is warning-free and matches the oracle on run, interp, and build.

The typed static test no longer classifies interned types through rendered strings. Correct fixture comments state the static/dynamic dispatch laws. Semantic fixpoint and type rustdocs state the conservative retained-key rule.

## Durable evidence

The detailed proof is `.agent/measurements/fz-kdt.169-capture-key-proof.md`. Ticket attachments preserve the rejected patch, three reconstruction/analyzer scripts, fixture list, retained/prototype behavior manifests, backend/claim/work mover tables, aggregate claim counts, and summary. The raw corpus, binaries, and gate logs are temporary construction artifacts and are deleted after acceptance.

## Acceptance result

- Rejected prototype: 607 fixtures across interp/run/build/AOT behavior phases, 7,284 normalized behavior entries per side, zero behavior/exit movers.
- Final candidate: inventory 1/1; typed static/dynamic semantics 2/2; erasure 1/1; same-shape sharing 1/1; centralized warning-totality 1/1; promoted fixture 3/3 warning-free doors plus real-Elixir oracle 1/1.
- Formatting/diff checks, strict all-target/all-feature clippy, doctests, `cargo test --lib` (1,961 passed, 6 ignored), and serial fixture matrix (540/540) pass.
- No production behavior logic is added. The candidate removes the duplicate root fixture and compile-only test/TODO.
- fz-kdt.185 owns the exact warning-free runtime contracts beneath this ticket; fz-tfn.58 separately owns the remaining 13 Enum private-list-walker warnings.

comments.text:
POPULATION MEASURED at the fz-kdt.127.2 landing (base 8c3d5ce90 vs head; 597
corpus fixtures x 3 doors, 469 backend dumps; 0 behaviour movers after
normalizing pids/thread ids/ASLR).

58 canon movers, 44 key-TEXT only. Of the 14 whose inventory moves, this
ticket's population -- a forwarder split by capture TUPLE across DIFFERENT
lambdas -- is EIGHT files / seven programs, and every one is the same shape: a
capture-FREE lambda keys apart from a capture-BEARING one, or two lambdas with
different capture arities do.

  00275_enum_count_member_reduce      25 -> 26 execs, dispatch 1 -> 0
    Enumerable.List.reduce/3: main/0#lambda@110-136 (0 captures, erases to the
    bare arrow) vs Enum.reduce/3#lambda@439-517 capturing the user reducer
    -> `(a2_p0, a2_p1) -> a2_r` vs `closure[?]((a2_p0, a2_p1) -> a2_r)`
  enum_map_family                     151 -> 152, dispatch 2 -> 2
    Enum.filter/2: a bare main/0 lambda vs Enum.reject/2#lambda@2097 capturing one
  mailbox_closure_each                29 -> 31, dispatch 0 -> 0
    Kernel.send/2 + fz_send/2: main/0#lambda@1140 (0 captures) vs
    main/0#lambda@1259 (`closure[?](int)`)
  mailbox_closure_reduce              39 -> 41, dispatch 0 -> 0   (same shape)
  actor_ring                          22 -> 24, dispatch 0 -> 0
    Kernel.spawn/1 + fz_spawn/1: main/0#lambda@466 `closure[?](pid)` vs
    relay/2#lambda@323 `closure[?](pid, int)` -- different capture ARITY, so
    provably different lambdas
  enum_predicate_search               204 -> 206, dispatch 3 -> 2
    Enum.reduce_while/3 + Enumerable.List.reduce_while/3 + List.reduce_while/3:
    capture-free Enum.all?/1 and any?/1 wrappers vs capturing all?/2 and any?/2
  enum_take_drop_split (x2 files)     196 -> 204, dispatch 0 -> 2
    the same chain: capture-free take_positive/drop_positive vs take_every/
    drop_every, which close over the step (`closure[?](int)`). THE ONLY
    FIXTURE THAT GAINS DISPATCH NODES, and both are real questions in the
    recursive core -- the accumulator tag `{:cont, _}` vs
    `{:cont | :halt, _}`, and which construction the reducer is.

fz-kdt.127's OWN population (one lambda at two capture types) is six fixtures,
and five of them LOSE a dispatch node: 00277 (180->181, 3->2), a_mixed
(28->29, 1->0), repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2 (21->22, 1->0),
callable_union_capture_containment (37->35 execs -- a NET LOSS -- 1->0),
same_lambda_two_capture_types (28->29, 2->0), and the dynamic twin
(26->30, 2->6 by design).

So the corpus-wide dispatch ledger is seven fixtures losing nodes and two
gaining. This ticket's question is therefore narrow and answerable: is capture
ARITY (or 'is there a capture at all') the right forwarder grain for the
capture-free-vs-capturing pairs above? Every one of them splits a forwarder
whose two callers differ only in whether the lambda closed over anything, and
in five of the seven programs the split buys nothing observable (dispatch
unchanged at 0). Re-pinned inventory numbers with cause live in
canon_test.rs::backend_inventory_width_stays_pinned_on_the_target_fixtures and
public_trace_test.rs::ANALYSIS_CLAIM_RATCHET.

title: Retain transported capture tuples after rejecting costlier flow-sensitive erasure
